summary.text: Nick Coffey, a Democrat who worked as a federal prosecutor in the Western District of Oklahoma, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Attorney General of Oklahoma to Jon Echols.
A fifth-generation Oklahoman and graduate of the University of Oklahoma College of Law, he handled drug-trafficking, money-laundering and firearms cases.

paragraphs.text: Coffey is a fifth-generation Oklahoman who lives in Oklahoma City and graduated from the University of Oklahoma College of Law.
He worked as a federal prosecutor in the Western District of Oklahoma and served on the Department of Justice's Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force.
Oklahoma Voice, which describes him as a former prosecutor, reported that he spent seven years as an Oklahoma City-based assistant U.S. attorney.
According to his campaign, he was named Prosecutor of the Year by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Oklahoma in 2024 and by Homeland Security Investigations in 2023.
Oklahoma Voice reported at his October 2025 campaign launch that it is his first political campaign.
In 2026 he was the Democratic nominee for attorney general, and his campaign priorities included rooting out public corruption, public safety, protecting children and watching taxpayer spending.
He received 44.7% of the vote to Jon Echols's 55.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
